A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 22-page versions of Adversarial Attacks on Data Attribution. Their main text, equations, three figures, thirteen tables, and Appendices A-D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of Shadow Attack and Outlier Attack in Section 6, with additional experiments and perturbation examples in Appendices C-D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original image-classification and text-generation experiments, including the appendix ablations and Tiny ImageNet results.

M1.justification: Shadow Attack and Outlier Attack retain the same objectives, components, and procedures in Sections 4-5 and Appendix B.3. The edits to their descriptions are grammatical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, Digits, CIFAR-10, Shakespeare, and Tiny ImageNet. The image-classification, text-generation, augmentation, and alternative compensation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the same random-perturbation baseline. Appendix C.3 and Table 9 retain FGSM for setting (a) and PGD for setting (d) as white-box oracle comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendices B-C retain the same data sizes, model configurations, training budgets, perturbation settings, and evaluation procedures. Compensation Share and Fraction of Change remain the evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The dataset-size and attribution-method ablations, white-box comparisons, augmentation tests, and correct-prediction compensation analyses in Appendix C are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same perturbation examples.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. No repeated-run or seed disclosures, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Tables 2-13 and Figure 3. For example, Tables 2 and 3 retain reported compensation-share ratios of 206.3%-456.1% and 185.2%-643.9%, respectively.

T1.justification: The definitions, objectives, Theorem 5.1, and Appendix A's formal theorem, lemmas, and proofs are unchanged. Adding an article to Assumption 3 does not alter its mathematical meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claims, threat model, two attack contributions, and claims about compensation inflation and adversarial vulnerability.

C2.justification: The outlier-bias explanation, applicability boundaries, and interpretations of the experiments remain unchanged. Appendix C.4 still finds no clear defensive effect from augmentation while concluding that the attacks remain effective.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same architectures, optimizers, learning rates, training durations, shadow-model counts, and attack hyperparameters. The implementation link and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The dattri reference changes from an arXiv entry to NeurIPS publication details and corrects its title formatting, but identifies the same work. The cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized grammar and punctuation corrections in Assumption 3, Section 6, and Appendices B.3 and C.4-C.6. It also cleans up the dattri bibliography entry and updates the version stamp. Section organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-3 and Tables 1-13 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. The overall page layout is unchanged apart from incidental local text reflow following copyediting.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves editorial quality through grammatical corrections and replacement of the malformed 'textttdattri' reference with a clean title and publication details. Methods, claims, proofs, and empirical evidence throughout the main text and appendices remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited to presentation.
